questions.stem: Suppose you are invited to put forward a proposal to the university on how to make students' campus life easier. You are now to write an essay to make your proposal. You will have 30 minutes to write the essay. You should write at least 120 words but not more than 180 words.
questions.analysis:
【参考范文】
I am honored to submit a proposal on how to make students' campus life easier. As daily routines grow more demanding, small improvements in campus services can save students considerable time and energy.

First, the university could develop a one-stop mobile app that integrates course schedules, room bookings, and exam arrangements. This would spare students the trouble of switching between multiple platforms. Second, extending library opening hours and adding more self-study spaces during examination periods would reduce overcrowding. Third, improving shuttle-bus frequency between teaching buildings and dormitories would make commuting less stressful.

These practical measures, if implemented, would significantly ease students' daily pressures. I sincerely hope the university will consider this proposal and take steps toward a more convenient campus life.

sections.title: Section II Listening Comprehension
sections.note: 本场次听力只有一份音频，本套听力与同场第一套同卷；原文、题目与答案取自该套真题。考场多套卷的选项顺序可能不同，这里沿用第一套的顺序。在线音频由语音合成朗读原文，不是考场录音；换浏览器、换手机都能播。

transcript.text: A man was left with a $1,000 bill, after his 6-year-old son ordered a virtual buffet of food from several restaurants last weekend. This led to a string of unexpected deliveries, and maybe a starring role in an advertisement campaign.
transcript.zh: 上周末，一名男子的6岁儿子从多家餐厅订购了一顿“虚拟自助餐”，结果给他留下了一张1000美元的账单。这引发了一连串意外送餐，也可能让他在一场广告宣传活动中担任主角。

transcript.text: Keith Stonehouse said the food piled up quickly at his home Saturday night, after he let his son use his cell phone to play a game before bed. He said the youngster instead used his father's online food ordering account to order food from one restaurant after another. The boy's mother, Christine Stonehouse, said that the online food app has reached out to the family and offered them a $1,000 gift card. The company also is considering using the family in an online promotional campaign.
transcript.zh: 基思·斯通豪斯说，上周六晚上，他让儿子睡前用自己的手机玩游戏，之后食物很快就堆满了家里。他说，孩子没有玩游戏，而是使用父亲的在线点餐账户，一家接一家地订购食物。男孩的母亲克里斯蒂娜·斯通豪斯说，这款在线点餐应用已经联系了他们一家，并向他们提供了一张价值1000美元的礼品卡。该公司还在考虑让这一家人参与一场线上宣传活动。

transcript.text: Most of the food went into the family's refrigerators. They also invited some neighbors over to eat some of it. The father is planning to change his password.
transcript.zh: 大部分食物都放进了家里的冰箱。他们还邀请了一些邻居来吃掉其中一部分。孩子的父亲打算更改密码。

questions.stem: Why was Keith Stonehouse left with a $1,000 bill?

options.text: He had bought meals with his online food ordering account.
His son had used his cell phone to pay for playing a game.
His son had ordered food from several restaurants.
He had dined out at a famous five-star restaurant.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：A man was left with a $1,000 bill, after his 6-year-old son ordered a virtual buffet of food from several restaurants last weekend.信号：after 因果链 。新闻首句用 after his 6-year-old son ordered... 直接交代了账单产生的原因：after 前面是结果（$1,000 bill），后面是原因（儿子点餐）。

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：录音确实出现了 'online food ordering account'，但用该账户点餐的是儿子，不是父亲；A 把动作主体从 son 偷换成 He，属于典型的主体张冠李戴。 借用原文：let his son use his cell phone to play a game
optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：录音提到父亲 'let his son use his cell phone to play a game'，但儿子实际上没玩游戏，而是去点餐了；B 把 'play a game' 偷换成 'pay for playing a game'，动作和目的都错了。
optionAnalysis.D: 未提及：录音从未提到 'five-star restaurant'，也未说父亲外出就餐；D 用高档餐厅制造生活常识诱惑，属于录音中找不到依据的干扰。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（his 6-year-old son ordered a virtual buffet of food from several restaurants ↔ His son had ordered food from several restaurants. 概括式同义替换）

questions.evidenceText: A man was left with a $1,000 bill, after his 6-year-old son ordered a virtual buffet of food from several restaurants last weekend.

questions.stem: What does the news report say Keith Stonehouse is planning to do?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P3）：The father is planning to change his password.信号：planning to 直接对应题干 。is planning to change his password 中的 'planning to' 与题干 'is planning to do' 完全同构，后面接的 'c…

optionAnalysis.A: 未提及：录音中没有出现 'teach his son a lesson' 或任何惩罚、教育的表述；A 是利用家长的'常识反应'编造的合理但无依据选项。
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：录音确实提到 'invited some neighbors over to eat some of it'，但目的是分享食物，不是 'ask his neighbors for help'；C 盗用 'neighbors' 一词并改变了动作性质。 借用原文：refrigerators
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：录音提到 'Most of the food went into the family's refrigerators'，但完全没有 'buy a bigger refrigerator' 的计划；D 用 'refrigerator' 这个原词做诱饵，把'已有冰箱'偷换成'要买更大的冰箱'。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（change his password ↔ Change his password. 原词复现 + 主语省略）

transcript.text: 1 Animal behaviour experts looked at more than 100 research papers.
They examined how visitors affected the behaviour of more than 250 species in zoos.
They found that elephants socialised more with each other during public feeding times.
After public feeding times, they were more likely to search for food and less likely to be inactive.

In the presence of many visitors, elephants were less likely to use repetitive behaviours which often indicate boredom. 2 Visitors had a similar effect on some other species too, including polar bears, certain jungle cats and black-tailed plain dogs.
Some animal species have been born and raised in zoos, and so have likely become used to the presence of humans.

Zoo visitors are often aspects of a zoo animal's environment that animals cannot control, and as such can be stressful, although some species appear to show good adaptability to the changing conditions of visitors.

questions.stem: What did animal behaviour experts do according to the news report?

options.text: They examined how visitors affected animal behaviour in zoos.
They studied when the best time to feed animals in public was.
They studied how animals adapted themselves to life in zoos.
They examined what behaviours indicated animal boredom.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：They examined how visitors affected the behaviour of more than 250 species in zoos.信号：直接陈述研究内容的动作句 。Paragraph 1 开头先说专家 looked at more than 100 research papers，紧接着 They examined how visitors affe…

optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：录音提到 during public feeding times 与 After public feeding times，但这是在说大象的行为变化，B 项把 public feeding times 改成 'the best time to feed animals'，既偷换概念又答非所问。 借用原文：good adaptability to the changing conditions of visitors
optionAnalysis.C: 偷换概念：some species appear to show good adaptability to the changing conditions of visitors 讲的是适应游客变化，C 项改成 'adapted themselves to life in zoos'，对象从 visitors 变成 zoos，属于偷换概念。 借用原文：repetitive behaviours which often indicate boredom
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：repetitive behaviours which often indicate boredom 只是研究中的一个发现细节，D 项把它上升为专家的研究主题 'what behaviours indicated animal boredom'。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（They examined how visitors affected the behaviour of more than 250 species in zoos. ↔ They examined how visitors affected animal behaviour in zoos. 具体数量概括为 animal，研究对象一致）

questions.evidenceText: They examined how visitors affected the behaviour of more than 250 species in zoos.

questions.stem: Why have some animal species likely become used to the presence of humans?

options.text: They socialise with zookeepers as well as with each other.
They show good adaptability to living with humans.
They have been kept as pets by humans.
They have been born and raised in zoos.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：Some animal species have been born and raised in zoos, and so have likely become used to the presence of humans.信号：因果连词 and so 把原因和结果钉在一起 。题干中的 'become used to the presence of humans' 与答案句后半句完全对应，前半句 'have been born and rai…

optionAnalysis.A: 张冠李戴：elephants socialised more with each other 是 Paragraph 1 中关于大象的发现，与题干问的 'some animal species' 习惯人类无关，且 zookeepers 在录音中从未出现。 借用原文：good adaptability to the changing conditions of visitors
optionAnalysis.B: 答非所问：录音确实提到 some species appear to show good adaptability to the changing conditions of visitors，但这是习惯人类之后表现出的能力，是结果；题干问 why，B 项答非所问。
optionAnalysis.C: 未提及：录音只说 born and raised in zoos 导致习惯人类存在，从未提到 as pets。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（have been born and raised in zoos ↔ They have been born and raised in zoos. 原因部分被原样截取，主语由 Some animal species 换成 They）

questions.evidenceText: Some animal species have been born and raised in zoos, and so have likely become used to the presence of humans.

transcript.text: 1 Denver is suspending its popular electric bike incentive program.
The program was launched in April.
It allowed Denver residents to apply for $400 in government funds before buying an electric bike from a participating shop.
Residents who met certain income qualifications could qualify for $1,200.
More than 3,000 Denver residents applied for incentives within the first 3 weeks. 2 The city then changed the program to limit the number of applications each month.
On Monday, the city announced the pause.
"We're honored to be a part of transforming the way Denver wants to move around," said Grace Rink, Denver's chief climate officer.
"We exhausted three years' worth of funding in six months." The city said the program has put 4,400 electric bikes on the streets of Denver and invested $8.6 million into the local economy.
The city has provided 2,200 incentives to lower-income residents that represent 68% of the program funding.
The city expects to resume the program early next year.
It also plans design changes to make participation easier and increase access to the program.

questions.stem: What is Denver doing with its popular electric bike incentive program?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：Denver is suspending its popular electric bike incentive program.信号：新闻首句直接点题 。Denver is suspending its popular electric bike incentive program 位于新闻首句，直接回答了 What is Denver doing…

optionAnalysis.A: 答非所问：选项 A 的 Adjusting 看似与原文 plans design changes 沾边，但 design changes 是 plan（计划），不是当前正在做的动作，且题干问的是 doing（现在进行）。 借用原文：increase access to the program
optionAnalysis.C: 未提及：选项 C 的 Reevaluating 在录音中没有对应表述，属于凭空捏造。
optionAnalysis.D: 偷换概念：选项 D 的 Expanding it 容易被 increase access to the program 诱惑，但 increase access 是 plans（未来设计目标），且项目当前是暂停而非扩张。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（is suspending ↔ Suspending it 现在进行时动作直接对应）

questions.evidenceText: Denver is suspending its popular electric bike incentive program.

questions.stem: How did the electric bike incentive program benefit residents?

options.text: They could buy an electric bike for $400 in April.
They could buy their first electric bike at a discount.
They could enjoy free after-sale service for their purchase.
They could get $1,200 from government funds if they qualified.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：It allowed Denver residents to apply for $400 in government funds before buying an electric bike from a participating shop. Residents who met certain income qualifications could qualify for $1,200.信号：居民获益的具体说明 。题干 benefit residents 问居民如何受益，原文 allowed Denver residents to apply for $400 和 Residents who met ce…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：选项 A 把 $400 in government funds 和 launched in April 两个原词拼凑成 buy an electric bike for $400 in April，但原文说的是申请 $400 资金，不是花 $400 买车；April 是项目启动时间，不是买车时间。 借用原文：buying an electric bike from a participating shop
optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：选项 B 盗用原文 buying an electric bike，但原文说的是申请政府补贴，不是直接打折；discount 在录音中并未出现。
optionAnalysis.C: 未提及：选项 C 的 after-sale service 在原文中没有对应内容，属于无中生有。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（Residents who met certain income qualifications could qualify for $1,200 ↔ They could get $1,200 from government funds if they qualified 同义替换：资格条件与获得资助的改写）

questions.evidenceText: It allowed Denver residents to apply for $400 in government funds before buying an electric bike from a participating shop. Residents who met certain income qualifications could qualify for $1,200.

questions.stem: What does the city of Denver expect to do early next year?

options.text: Put 400 more electric bikes on its streets.
Increase the program funding by 8 percent.
Resume its electric bike incentive program.
Invest millions of dollars into the local economy.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：The city expects to resume the program early next year.信号：题干关键词直接复现 。原文 expects to resume the program early next year 与题干 expect to do early next year 的关键词 expects / …

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：选项 A 把 $400 和 put 4,400 electric bikes on the streets 拼凑成 Put 400 more electric bikes on its streets，数字和时态都错了。 借用原文：68% of the program funding
optionAnalysis.B: 偷换概念：选项 B 的 8 percent 在原文中没有依据，可能是把 68% of the program funding 误听或篡改而来。 借用原文：invested $8.6 million into the local economy
optionAnalysis.D: 与原文相反：选项 D 盗用原文 invested $8.6 million into the local economy，但原文用的是 invested（已完成），而题干问的是 expect to do early next year（未来计划），时态不符。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（expects to resume the program early next year ↔ Resume its electric bike incentive program 同义替换：resume the program = Resume its electric bike incentive program）

questions.evidenceText: The city expects to resume the program early next year.

transcript.text: W: Hey, Mike, what do you think of the museum you visited today?
transcript.zh: W: 嘿，迈克，你觉得今天参观的博物馆怎么样？

transcript.text: M: Hey, Sue. The museum is great, very interesting. They have loads of stuff there on display. The primitive tools early humans used tell a lot about their life, but my favorite is the coin collection. They have some coins that are over 2,000 years old.
transcript.zh: M: 嘿，苏。这个博物馆很棒，非常有意思。那里展出了很多东西。早期人类使用的原始工具能让我们了解到很多他们的生活情况，不过我最喜欢的是钱币收藏。他们有些钱币已经有两千多年的历史了。

transcript.text: W: That sounds cool.
transcript.zh: W: 听起来很酷。

transcript.text: M: Yeah, what did you do today?
transcript.zh: M: 是啊，你今天做了什么？

transcript.text: W: Kathy and I just wandered through the old city centre. The streets are narrow but beautiful with plenty of charm. We saw the Trevi Fountain, which is in all the guidebooks.
transcript.zh: W: 我和凯西只是逛了逛老城区。街道虽然狭窄，却很漂亮，充满了魅力。我们看了特莱维喷泉，所有旅游指南上都有介绍。

transcript.text: M: How do you like it?
transcript.zh: M: 你觉得怎么样？

transcript.text: W: It's very pretty, but it was overcrowded with tourists.
transcript.zh: W: 非常漂亮，不过游客太多了，挤得水泄不通。

transcript.text: M: Yeah, well, it's crowded everywhere. It is August after all, the busiest month of the year.
transcript.zh: M: 是啊，到处都很拥挤。毕竟现在是八月，一年中最繁忙的月份。

transcript.text: W: Yes, it's like the whole world is here on holiday, including us. What will you do tomorrow?
transcript.zh: W: 是啊，感觉全世界的人都来这里度假了，包括我们。你明天打算做什么？

transcript.text: M: I haven't decided yet. I was thinking of doing what you did today—wandering the old streets and taking pictures. I was also thinking of visiting the square with the Spanish steps.
transcript.zh: M: 我还没决定。我在考虑做你今天做的事，逛逛老街，拍拍照。我还在考虑去看看有西班牙阶梯的那个广场。

transcript.text: W: What is that? I haven't heard of it.
transcript.zh: W: 那是什么地方？我没听说过。

transcript.text: M: It's a square where on one side, there are some very wide steps with flowers that go up to a church. It's also in all the tourist guidebooks. It's very famous and pretty. I was also thinking of seeing that tomorrow.
transcript.zh: M: 那是一个广场，广场一侧有一段很宽的台阶，台阶上摆满了鲜花，一直通向一座教堂。旅游指南上也都有介绍。那里非常有名，也很漂亮。我也在考虑明天去看看。

transcript.text: W: It sounds very nice. Do you mind if Kathy and I join you tomorrow?
transcript.zh: W: 听起来很不错。你介意明天我和凯西跟你一起去吗？

transcript.text: M: Not at all. I spent the whole day today pretty much alone. Doing tourist stuff with others would be a welcome change.
transcript.zh: M: 当然不介意。我今天基本上独自待了一整天。和别人一起做些游客会做的事，换换方式也挺不错的。

transcript.text: W: Let me ask her first, but I'm sure she'll be up for it.
transcript.zh: W: 我先问问她，不过我相信她会愿意去的。

questions.stem: What exhibits does the man like best in the museum he visited?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：The primitive tools early humans used tell a lot about their life, but my favorite is the coin collection.信号：转折 but + favorite 点出最爱 。男士先提 The primitive tools，随即用 but my favorite is 把重点转向 coin collection，favorite 与题干 l…

optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：The primitive tools. 确实出现在 The primitive tools early humans used...，但它是 but 之前的铺垫，与 like best 无关。 借用原文：some coins that are over 2,000 years old
optionAnalysis.C: 未提及：录音中只提到 tools 与 coin collection，完全没有 ornaments 这一展品。
optionAnalysis.D: 偷换概念：The 2,000-year-old clothes. 盗用了 over 2,000 years old 这一数字，但原文说的是 coins，不是 clothes。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（my favorite is the coin collection ↔ The coin collection. favorite = like best）

questions.evidenceText: The primitive tools early humans used tell a lot about their life, but my favorite is the coin collection.

questions.stem: What does the woman say about the old city centre?

options.text: It is charming with narrow but beautiful streets.
It attracts visitors from every corner of the world.
It has flowers displayed around the Trevi Fountain.
It is more attractive than the pictures in guidebooks.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P5）：The streets are narrow but beautiful with plenty of charm.信号：直接描述 + but 强调 beautiful/charm 。女士用 narrow but beautiful with plenty of charm 直接描述 old city centre 的街道，but 后的…

optionAnalysis.B: 张冠李戴：It attracts visitors from every corner of the world. 盗用 it's like the whole world is here on holiday，但这是对整个城市旺季的感受，不是 old city centre 本身。 借用原文：with flowers that go up to a church
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：It has flowers displayed around the Trevi Fountain. 盗用 with flowers，但 flowers 是在 Spanish steps 的台阶上，不是 Trevi Fountain 周围。 借用原文：in all the guidebooks
optionAnalysis.D: 过度推断：It is more attractive than the pictures in guidebooks. 中的 guidebooks 出现在 in all the guidebooks，但女士只说 Trevi Fountain 上了 guidebooks，并未比较吸引力。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（The streets are narrow but beautiful with plenty of charm ↔ It is charming with narrow but beautiful streets. charm→charming，同词保留 narrow but beautiful）

questions.evidenceText: The streets are narrow but beautiful with plenty of charm.

questions.stem: What does the man say about the square with the Spanish steps?

options.text: It is covered with wild grass.
It is very famous and pretty.
It is located away from an old church.
It is surrounded by Spanish-style houses.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P12）：It's a square where on one side, there are some very wide steps with flowers that go up to a church. It's also in all the tourist guidebooks. It's very famous and pretty.信号：连续介绍后 famous/pretty 给出评价 。男士先说明 square 的物理特征，再用 It's very famous and pretty. 给出总体评价，这是问题的直接回答。

optionAnalysis.A: 未提及：录音提到 wide steps with flowers，完全没有 wild grass。
optionAnalysis.C: 与原文相反：It is located away from an old church. 与 steps with flowers that go up to a church 相反。 借用原文：visiting the square with the Spanish steps
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：It is surrounded by Spanish-style houses. 盗用 Spanish 一词，但原文只说 square with the Spanish steps，未提 surrounding houses。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（It's very famous and pretty. ↔ It is very famous and pretty. It's → It is 缩写展开，形容词原词保留）

questions.evidenceText: It's a square where on one side, there are some very wide steps with flowers that go up to a church. It's also in all the tourist guidebooks. It's very famous and pretty.

questions.stem: What does the woman say she is going to do first?

options.text: Ask Kathy what her plan is.
Tell Kathy Mike will join them.
Ask Kathy if she'd like to see the square.
Tell Kathy Mike would like to have a change.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P15）：Let me ask her first, but I'm sure she'll be up for it.信号：first 直接对应题干 first 。女士用 Let me ask her first 明确动作的先后顺序，first 与题干 first 同词对应。

optionAnalysis.A: 答非所问：Ask Kathy what her plan is. 把 ask her 曲解为询问计划，但前文已计划去看 square，实际问的是愿不愿意加入。
optionAnalysis.B: 偷换概念：Tell Kathy Mike will join them. 把 ask 偷换成 tell，且 Kathy 是否加入尚未确定，不能提前告知。
optionAnalysis.D: 张冠李戴：Tell Kathy Mike would like to have a change. 盗用 Doing tourist stuff with others would be a welcome change，但这是 Mike 的想法，不是女士要 first 做的事。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（Let me ask her first ↔ Ask Kathy if she'd like to see the square. ask her → Ask Kathy；语境指约她看 square）

questions.evidenceText: Let me ask her first, but I'm sure she'll be up for it.

transcript.text: M: Can you give me advice about being successful at a new job? I start mine next week.
transcript.zh: M: 你能给我一些关于如何在新工作中取得成功的建议吗？我下周就要开始工作了。

transcript.text: W: Sure. It's important not to undermine the significance of the first few days of your job, since this is the best time to create a solid first impression.
transcript.zh: W: 当然。千万不要低估入职头几天的重要性，因为这段时间最适合树立良好的第一印象。

transcript.text: M: That's a good point. I'll need to collaborate with my coworkers and I'm very aware of just how important others are for my success at work.
transcript.zh: M: 你说得有道理。我需要和同事合作，而且我非常清楚别人对我在工作中的成功有多么重要。

transcript.text: W: It's also important to understand your role thoroughly to gain a comprehensive picture of your job. The most important thing for you to do at first is to understand your role from multiple perspectives.
transcript.zh: W: 彻底了解自己的职责也很重要，这样才能全面了解你的工作。你一开始最重要的事情，就是从多个角度了解自己的职责。

transcript.text: M: Why is that?
transcript.zh: M: 为什么呢？

transcript.text: W: Well, what you do at work is not just limited to your job description. You need to consider how your work relates to other people within the organization.
transcript.zh: W: 这个嘛，你在工作中做的事情并不只是局限于职位描述。你需要考虑自己的工作与组织内部其他人的工作有什么联系。

transcript.text: M: Oh, right. So, for example, certain reports that I create at the end of the month may be used by a team in another department.
transcript.zh: M: 哦，对。比如说，我在月底制作的某些报告可能会被另一个部门的团队使用。

transcript.text: W: That's right. And in that respect, it's also important to learn about the business to see the big picture.
transcript.zh: W: 没错。从这个角度来说，了解公司业务、掌握全局也很重要。

transcript.text: M: You mean like knowing about the history of the company.
transcript.zh: M: 你的意思是要了解公司的历史之类的吗？

transcript.text: W: Kind of, but more like knowing the details of the products and services that the company exists to deliver. Learning about the business will give you a chance to understand how your role fits into the bigger picture.
transcript.zh: W: 算是吧，不过更重要的是了解公司赖以存在的那些产品和服务的具体情况。了解公司业务能让你明白自己的职责是如何融入更大的整体的。

transcript.text: M: Okay. I'm feeling a bit uneasy about meeting my boss as well.
transcript.zh: M: 好的。不过，想到要见我的老板，我还是有点不安。

transcript.text: W: That's to be expected. However, it's crucial that you get to know the people who have decision-making authority to gain insight regarding how the business is run and decisions are made.
transcript.zh: W: 这是可以理解的。不过，了解那些拥有决策权的人至关重要，这样你才能深入了解公司是如何运营的，以及决策是如何做出的。

transcript.text: M: Great advice. Thanks.
transcript.zh: M: 这个建议太好了。谢谢。

transcript.text: Contrary to popular belief, consumers aren't as smart as they like to believe. Many consumers report comparing multiple competing brands and prices when evaluating a purchase. However, research indicates that this is not actually the case. What consumers really think or feel often contradicts what they say. A big reason is that they are driven by unconscious urges, the biggest of which is emotion.
transcript.zh: 与普遍看法相反，消费者并没有他们自认为的那么聪明。许多消费者表示，在评估一项购买时，他们会比较多个相互竞争的品牌及其价格。然而，研究表明，实际情况并非如此。消费者真正的想法或感受往往与他们所说的相矛盾。一个重要原因是，他们受到无意识冲动的驱使，其中最主要的就是情感。

transcript.text: Emotion is what really drives the purchasing behaviors, and also, decision making in general. Good marketers keep in mind this important fact all the time, and examples of emotion-based campaigns are everywhere. Think for a moment, what is actually being sold in most marketing campaigns? Luxury goods target our feelings of self-worth, acceptance, and status in the world. Communication devices excite us by offering a connection to friends, family and a broader network of people. And many other products, such as rings, target emotions related to love and relationships.
transcript.zh: 真正驱动购买行为的，是情感；一般而言，决策也是如此。优秀的营销人员始终牢记这一重要事实，而以情感为基础的营销活动随处可见。请想一想，大多数营销活动实际上销售的是什么？奢侈品瞄准的是我们关于自我价值、认同感以及社会地位的感受。通信设备通过提供与朋友、家人以及更广泛人际网络的联系，使我们感到兴奋。许多其他产品，例如戒指，则瞄准与爱情和人际关系相关的情感。

transcript.text: As marketers, we should focus on the features of the product, but we must also sell the lifestyle and the feeling. The key is to highlight the emotional response a consumer will have by using the product. To achieve the highest emotional response, we should target our consumer through many different senses. A lot of what drives consumers is subconscious behavior. But this isn't a bad thing. There's nothing manipulative about helping consumers achieve desired states of emotion.
transcript.zh: 作为营销人员，我们应当关注产品的功能，但也必须销售一种生活方式和一种感受。关键在于突出消费者使用产品后将产生的情感反应。为了达到最强烈的情感反应，我们应当通过许多不同的感官来触达消费者。驱动消费者行为的诸多因素都属于潜意识行为。但这并不是一件坏事。帮助消费者获得期望的情感状态，并没有任何操纵性。

transcript.text: Plastics have for years been used to make nearly everything that surrounds us. But along the way, they escaped the confines of packaging and objects and settled in the environment, the food we eat and the air we breathe.
transcript.zh: 多年来，塑料一直被用于制造我们周围几乎所有的东西。但在这一过程中，它们逃离了包装和物品的束缚，进入了环境、我们所吃的食物以及所呼吸的空气中。

transcript.text: Americans are consuming and breathing in a lot of plastic. Based on available data, Americans take in an estimated 74,000 to 121,000 microplastic particles every year. However, scientists believe the true number is probably much higher, because for some likely sources of microplastics, there were no strong data available.
transcript.zh: 美国人正在摄入并吸入大量塑料。根据现有数据估算，美国人每年摄入的微塑料颗粒数量在7.4万至12.1万之间。然而，科学家认为真实数量可能高得多，因为对于一些很可能的微塑料来源，目前没有可靠的数据。

transcript.text: Microplastics get into food and air in several ways. Many start off as part of larger plastic objects, which over time fragment into smaller and smaller pieces until they become tiny: 5 millimeters or less in diameter. They are breathed in or consumed by animals, and then become our food. The particles float through the air until people breathe them in. They also settle on the food that people eat.
transcript.zh: 微塑料通过多种方式进入食物和空气。许多微塑料最初是较大塑料物品的一部分，随着时间的推移逐渐碎裂成越来越小的碎片，最终变得十分微小，直径仅为5毫米或更小。它们会被动物吸入或摄入，随后成为我们的食物。这些颗粒漂浮在空气中，直到人们将其吸入。它们也会沉积在供人们食用的食物上。

transcript.text: Data shows that for Americans, air, bottled water and seafood were the biggest sources for breathed-in or consumed microplastics. Added sugars accounted for less, and salts, tap water and beer contributed minimal amounts. These estimates are conservative. The included foods only make up about 15% of the average American diet. It's not yet known how much plastic is contained in the remaining 85% of the typical diet.
transcript.zh: 数据显示，对于美国人来说，空气、瓶装水和海鲜是吸入或摄入微塑料的最大来源。添加糖所占比例较小，而盐、自来水和啤酒所贡献的数量极少。这些估算是保守的。所纳入的食物仅约占美国人平均饮食的15%。典型饮食中剩余的85%含有多少塑料，目前尚不清楚。

transcript.text: People looking to stay well as they age may want to adopt a pet animal, according to new data from the University of Michigan National Poll on Healthy Aging. For the survey, researchers polled about 2,000 U.S. adults from ages 50 to 80. 55% said they owned at least one pet. Dogs were the most common pet, followed by cats. But whatever the type of animal, the vast majority of owners said their pets boosted their mental and physical health.
transcript.zh: 密歇根大学健康老龄化全国民意调查的最新数据显示，希望随着年龄增长保持健康的人或许可以考虑养一只宠物。调查中，研究人员询问了约2,000名年龄在50至80岁之间的美国成年人。55%的人表示自己至少养有一只宠物。狗是最常见的宠物，其次是猫。但无论饲养何种动物，绝大多数宠物主人都表示，宠物改善了他们的心理和身体健康。

transcript.text: Nearly 90% of older pet owners said their animals helped them enjoy life and feel loved; roughly 80% said their pets reduced stress; and almost three-quarters said their pets provided a sense of purpose. paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: These days, phone interviews are an unavoidable part of the job interview process, and for good reason: They save time and effort. But that doesn't mean that phone calls require zero energy on the part of the candidate. Many companies treat phone screening as the official first round of the hiring process. That means candidates are expected to go into them prepared with as much information as possible about the company, position, and their own skills and strengths.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: A big mistake people often make is talking about their personal lives. Don't talk about your personal life unless you're directly asked a question about what you like to do in your off-hours. "The point of a phone interview is to focus on getting to know a candidate's professional experience and goals," says Mckenzie Roark, campus talent specialist at Lithko Contracting. "A recruiter is trying to see if they are the best fit for a role, and learning about their personal life doesn't help. For example, when asked where you see yourself in five years, we don't want to know that you hope to be married or that you want to buy a new house. That is nice, but that isn't relative to anything professional."

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: It might be tempting to cross something off your to-do list while on a phone interview, but recruiters and hiring managers can easily tell if your attention is elsewhere. Many interviewers are annoyed to see people who decide to multitask while on the phone interview. There are candidates who wash dishes, go for walks, or do grocery shopping during the interview. Needless to say, this doesn't reflect well on your level of interest in the position you're interviewing for.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: The question regarding pay is also best avoided. To be frank, it's simply too early in the process for you to be the one who brings up salary expectations. "Chances are if a candidate is participating in a phone interview, this is the first time they have talked with the company, and the first call isn't the appropriate time to talk about 'what's in it for you,'" says Justina Strnad, the Talent Acquisition Manager for Shiftgig. "Trust me, if you are a great candidate and make it to the next step, the hiring team is going to be very transparent about what's in it for you later on."

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: "After wrapping up a phone interview, it is typical that the interviewer will ask the candidate if they have any questions. I can't stress this enough: ALWAYS ask questions," says Roark. "If we have had a great phone interview and then we wrap up and they don't have any questions for me, it pretty much ruins the whole interview. It tells me that the candidate is uninterested in the role, which in reality might not be the case at all," she notes. But surely, if you're interested in a job, you can think of something to ask your interviewer.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: It seems basic, but surprisingly, a lot of people are late to phone interviews. "About a quarter of the people with whom I schedule phone interviews aren't on time," says Sophie Cikovsky, who handles U.S. recruiting for Infinite Global. "While this bothers me personally, it's also indicative of someone who isn't very detail-oriented," she explains. "In order to identify this early in the hiring process, I started asking all candidates a few years ago to call me as opposed to calling them at an agreed-upon time. That way, if I hear from them at 1:13 p.m. or 12:49 p.m. instead of our planned 1:00 p.m. interview time, I have an early indicator that they might not be a great fit."

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: "Make sure you test your headset and connection before dialing in," recommends Roark. "There is nothing more frustrating for a recruiter who has a structured interview guide in place having to repeatedly ask the same question over and over because they could not understand your answer due to dropped signals." Test-call a friend beforehand, or even call yourself from a landline if necessary; it will take less than a minute.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: You might be eager to get your point across or talk about your experience, but interrupting the interviewer is awkward and rude. "Interviewing can be stressful, and sometimes that stress manifests itself in speaking too fast, speaking too loud, talking over the interviewer, or attempting to answer the interviewer's question before they have actually finished asking the question," says Chris Dardis, a recruiting expert. "Don't do this." There's a big difference between being assertive(自信的) and being aggressive, and interviewers can always recognize it.

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: It's tough not to say things like "um," "uh," and "like" in everyday speech, but these verbal habits become much more pronounced when speaking on the phone, says Dardis. "In face-to-face interviews, they're not as noticeable, because there are other things like your hair, suit, or body language to distract people." But in a phone interview, the only thing you have to go on is what you say and how you say it. "That's why it's so important to eliminate these words from your speech when doing a phone interview."

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: Not knowing anything about the company or job you're interviewing for is way more obvious than you'd think. "Many people think that they don't have to put as much effort into researching the role or the company," says Steve Pritchard, an HR consultant. And if you have your laptop in front of you during the interview to do a few quick searches, they won't know the difference, right? Not exactly. "Seasoned interviewers will know whether an interviewee is researching while on the phone. The interviewer can often even hear the typing as they ask the question," he adds.

paragraphs.label: K
paragraphs.text: "The key to success during a phone interview is clear and concise answers," says Dardis. "People's attention spans tend to be shorter over the phone. You don't want your future employer to lose interest in the conversation." He recommends practicing answers to questions you know will be asked ahead of time in order to be clear on what you're going to say. That way, you can prevent talking in an aimless manner.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: After finding out details about a stranger, we mistakenly think that they also know about us. As a result, we act more honestly around them, according to a recent study in Nature.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Past research has found that we tend to assume social relationships are reciprocal(相互的). Most of the time, this assumption is accurate: someone you think of as a friend will usually consider you a friend too. But sometimes our social ties are more one-sided: for example, you might learn something about a stranger who doesn't know you at all. Researchers Anuj Shah and Michael LaForest wondered whether our tendency to believe that social ties are reciprocal could lead us to mistakenly feel that a stranger does actually know us.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: In a series of lab-based studies, this is exactly what the researchers found. When we know about strangers, we erroneously think they also know about us. But the really interesting finding came when the researchers stepped out of the lab, to conduct a field experiment. The team developed leaflets(传单) containing fairly ordinary information about local community police officers, such as their favourite food, hobbies, or reasons for joining the police force. They then sent out these leaflets to every apartment in a number of housing developments in disadvantaged areas. The officers themselves also dropped off cards to local residents containing similar information.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Two months later, the researchers surveyed residents at these housing developments as well as control areas that did not receive leaflets or outreach cards. Residents were asked to imagine that they had committed a crime and how likely it would be that local officers would find out about it. They also rated how well the officers in the area knew them.

paragraphs.label: E

Even more strikingly, the team found that immediately after the leaflet distribution, there were fewer criminal complaints and arrests in the areas around the developments that had received the leaflets than around the control developments.
